nodes.characterization_summary: W-Co3O4 and Co3O4 show same spinel crystalline structure with no W species peaks such as WO3 (Fig. S1a); W-Co3O4 (311) peak shifts to higher angle indicating lattice contraction by W doping (Fig. S1b).
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-Ray diffraction (XRD) showed the same crystalline structure in W–Co3O4 and Co3O4, with no diffraction peaks associated with W species, such as WO3 (Fig. S1a, ESI†). This implies the highly dispersed W species in W–Co3O4. The major (311) diffraction peak of W–Co3O4 shifts to a higher angle compared with that of Co3O4, indicative of lattice contraction aroused by W doping (Fig. S1b, ESI†).

nodes.characterization_summary: W-Co3O4 and Co3O4 show four characteristic Raman peaks for spinel structure with no extra phase peaks (Fig. S2).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Raman spectra of W–Co3O4 and Co3O4 showed four characteristic Raman peaks for spinel structure, and no other extra phase peaks were found (Fig. S2, ESI†).

nodes.characterization_summary: W-Co3O4 nanoparticles average diameter 14.04±0.18 nm (Fig. 1a inset); Co3O4 nanoparticles average size 14.4±0.46 nm (Fig. S3) with similar morphology and high crystallinity (Fig. S4).
nodes.evidence_snippet: Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) clearly showed that W–Co3O4 nanoparticles with an average diameter of 14.04±0.18 nm (Fig. 1a, inset). The Co3O4 catalysts showed morphology similar to that of W–Co3O4, with an average nanoparticle size of 14.4±0.46 nm (Fig. S3, ESI†), as well as high crystallinity (Fig. S4, ESI†).

nodes.characterization_summary: Atomic dispersion of W single atoms on Co3O4 surface confirmed; no clusters or nanoparticles detected.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The spherical aberration-corrected STEM (Cs-corrected STEM) image shows the atomic dispersion of W on the surface of Co3O4... By observing the Cs-corrected STEM image of different faces of W–Co3O4, no clusters or nanoparticles were detected and single atoms with brighter intensity contrast were clearly distinguished

nodes.characterization_summary: O K-edge of W-Co3O4 shows pre-edge peak shift to higher energy loss and lower intensity vs Co3O4 indicating higher O vacancy concentration; Co L-edge shows decreased L3/L2 ratio and L3 peak shift to lower energy indicating lower Co valence.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In the O K-edge EELS spectra, the pre-edge peak of W–Co3O4 shifted to higher energy loss, and lower intensity... the Co L-edge EELS spectra show that the ratio of the Co L3/L2 feature is decreased and the L3 peak shifted to lower energy loss compared to pure Co3O4

nodes.characterization_summary: Homogeneous dispersion of W, Co, and O atoms throughout W-Co3O4 sample.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Elemental mapping images showed a homogeneous dispersion of W, Co, and O atoms throughout the entire W–Co3O4 sample

nodes.characterization_summary: W 4f binding energies in W-Co3O4 negatively shifted 0.1 eV vs WO3 indicating lower W oxidation state; Co3+:Co2+ ratio 1.12:1 in W-Co3O4 vs 1.29:1 in Co3O4; O 1s shows higher lattice oxygen and oxygen vacancies (28.3% vs 19.5%) in W-Co3O4.
nodes.evidence_snippet: For high-resolution W 4f XPS spectra, the binding energy of W 4f7/2 and 4f5/2 for W–Co3O4 was negatively shifted (0.1 eV) compared to that of WO3... The Co 2p XPS spectra revealed a high ratio of Co2+:Co3+ in W–Co3O4 (the ratio of Co3+:Co2+ in W–Co3O4 and Co3O4 are 1.12:1 and 1.29:1 respectively)... the O 1s spectra of W–Co3O4 showed... oxygen vacancies (W–Co3O4 and Co3O4 are 28.3% and 19.5%, respectively)

nodes.characterization_summary: Number of oxygen vacancies increased after W atoms introduction in W-Co3O4 vs Co3O4.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) spectra further revealed the number of oxygen vacancies increased after W atoms were introduced

nodes.characterization_summary: Co K-edge XANES of W-Co3O4 shows slightly red-shifted absorption vs Co3O4 indicating lower Co oxidation state; W L-edge white line shifts 1.6 eV higher than W foil, closer to WO3 indicating W state slightly lower than +6.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The XANES spectrum at the Co K-edge (W–Co3O4) shows a very similar spectral pattern to that of Co3O4 with a slightly red-shifted absorption energy... The XANES spectrum at the W L-edge can observe that the white line of W–Co3O4 shifts by 1.6 eV to a higher energy relative to W foil, but is located closer to WO3

nodes.characterization_summary: W-Co3O4 shows lower intensities and coordination numbers for Co-O and Co-Co shells vs Co3O4; W L-edge shows W-O at 1.40 Å (vs 1.35 Å in WO3), no W-W bonding confirming atomic dispersion of W single atoms.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Compared with Co3O4, the EXAFS of W–Co3O4 shows lower intensities and CNs corresponding to Co–O and Co–Co shells... The information derived from W L-edge EXAFS shows... some appreciable shift of W–O peak (1.40 Å) for W–Co3O4... The lack of W–W bonding at 2.60 Å proves the atomic dispersion of single W atoms
